notes: This proof uses a loopback webserver and deterministic local scanner binaries on isolated PATH.
The model endpoint is a real Qwen app engine route; the web scanners are local fixtures for deterministic safety.
PASS requires q4 TurboQuant KV, hybrid_ssm_typed native cache, paged cache, prefix cache, block disk cache, and SSM rederive without failures.
The SSRF and file-read validation uses harmless local fixture canaries only; it does not access cloud metadata or host-sensitive files.

Client: Unknown

Assessor: exploitbot (autonomous)
Classification: Confidential

1. Executive Summary

A penetration test was conducted against Unknown. The assessment identified 1 vulnerabilities including 0 critical, 1 high, 0 medium, and 0 low severity findings.

2. Findings Summary

#FindingSeverityCVSSTargetStatus
1SSRF and file-read in local fixtureHIGH8.0http://127.0.0.1:50578/fetch?url=...confirmed

3. Detailed Findings

HIGH SSRF and file-read in local fixture

Target: http://127.0.0.1:50578/fetch?url=...

CVSS: 8.0

Description: The local fixture fetch endpoint reaches a loopback canary and the download endpoint reads a fixture file.

Impact

An attacker could pivot request targets or read unintended local fixture files if this pattern existed in production.

Remediation

Use strict outbound URL allowlists, block loopback/private networks, and constrain file reads to known fixture paths.
